plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 9: Linear Momentum and Collisions
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional drawing of a single cubic unit cell of a sodium chloride crystal set on a coordinate frame. Solid black axes emerge from a corner labeled 0 at the lower left, with x running toward the lower right, y toward the upper right, and z straight up, each ending in an arrowhead beside its italic label. Dashed orange lines trace the edges of the cube. Eight shaded spheres sit at the corners in two alternating colors, each tagged with a subscripted mass symbol. The green spheres are m_1 at the origin, m_3 at the far corner of the xy face, m_6 at the far corner of the xz face, and m_8 at the far corner of the yz face. The red spheres are m_2 out along the x-axis, m_4 out along the y-axis, m_5 up the z-axis, and m_7 at the corner diagonally opposite the origin. The alternation of the two colors around every face shows that no two like-colored ions share an edge, and numbering all eight corners while anchoring the origin on one of them supplies the labeled coordinates needed to work out the center of mass of the eight-particle cell.

elements: Solid black x-axis from origin running toward lower-right with arrowhead and italic label 'x'
Solid black y-axis from origin running toward upper-right with arrowhead and italic label 'y'
Solid black z-axis from origin running straight up with arrowhead and italic label 'z'
Label '0' at the origin corner (lower-left)
Cube unit cell of side a, one corner exactly at the origin, edges aligned with +x, +y, +z
Twelve cube edges drawn as dashed orange lines (the three edges lying along the axes are overdrawn by the solid black axis lines)
Green sphere m1 at (0,0,0), the origin corner
Red sphere m2 at (a,0,0), out along the x-axis
Green sphere m3 at (a,a,0), far corner of the bottom xy face
Red sphere m4 at (0,a,0), out along the y-axis
Red sphere m5 at (0,0,a), up the z-axis
Green sphere m6 at (a,0,a), far corner of the xz (y=0) face
Red sphere m7 at (a,a,a), the corner diagonally opposite the origin
Green sphere m8 at (0,a,a), far corner of the yz (x=0) face
Subscripted mass labels m1..m8 placed beside each sphere (m5 left of its sphere, m8 above, m7 upper-right, m6 lower-right, m4 right, m3 right, m2 below, m1 below-left)
Soft shading/specular highlight on each sphere giving it a ball-like 3D appearance

interactions.teaches: The eight labeled masses really sit on the corners of one cube; rotating shows which spheres are near versus far and confirms that green and red ions strictly alternate along every edge in all three directions.
Pointing at a corner names that ion, shows its (x, y, z) coordinate in units of the cube edge a, and reports its color group — tying the label m_i to a definite position for the center-of-mass sum.

interactions.label: Emphasis
interactions.teaches: Switching emphasis separates the physical crystal fact — two alternating ion species, no two like ions sharing an edge — from the bookkeeping view, where the same eight corners are just numbered masses with coordinates to feed into the center-of-mass formula.

demo_steps.title: The unit cell on the axes
demo_steps.narration: A cube of edge a sits with one corner at the origin, its edges running along x, y and z. Dashed orange lines outline the cell.

demo_steps.title: Alternating ions
demo_steps.narration: Green and red spheres alternate around every face: m1, m3, m6 and m8 are one species, m2, m4, m5 and m7 the other. No two like-colored ions ever share an edge.

demo_steps.title: Eight masses with coordinates
demo_steps.narration: Now the same corners read as numbered masses m1 through m8. Hover any sphere to see its coordinate — (0,0,0), (a,0,0), (a,a,0), (0,a,0), (0,0,a), (a,0,a), (a,a,a), (0,a,a) — the data needed for the center-of-mass sum.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cube edge a = 2.0 world units, corner m1 at the world origin, cube occupying x,y,z in [0,2]. Axes are solid black lines from the origin out to 3.0 units along +x (screen lower-right), +y (screen upper-right) and +z (screen up), each capped with a small cone arrowhead and an italic label just past the tip. Corner coordinates in units of a: m1(0,0,0) green, m2(1,0,0) red, m3(1,1,0) green, m4(0,1,0) red, m5(0,0,1) red, m6(1,0,1) green, m7(1,1,1) red, m8(0,1,1) green. Sphere radius ≈ 0.22 (about 11% of the edge), all eight equal. Colors: green ions #7CB342 with lighter #A5D66B highlight; red ions #C0392B with #E06055 highlight; cube edges dashed orange #E8642A (dash ~0.12, gap ~0.10); axes, arrowheads and text black #111111. Center of mass, if shown, is at (a/2, a/2, a/2) only when all eight masses are equal; otherwise R = (Σ m_i r_i)/(Σ m_i). Label offsets follow the source: m5 to the left of its sphere, m8 above, m7 upper-right, m6 lower-right, m4 to the right, m3 to the right, m2 below, m1 below-left, and '0' just left of the origin.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera in a standard isometric pose so cube edges stay parallel, matching the flat drafting look of the source. Spheres: MeshStandardMaterial with moderate roughness plus one key directional light from the upper left and a soft ambient fill to reproduce the shaded-ball look. Dashed cube edges: LineSegments with LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) — draw all twelve edges dashed, then overlay the three origin-adjacent edges with the solid black axis lines so the axes read on top. Labels as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so subscripts render crisply and always face the camera during orbit. Hover: raycast against the eight sphere meshes; on hit, scale the sphere ~1.25x, add an emissive rim, drop faint guide lines to its x, y and z axis projections, and show a tooltip with the mass symbol, coordinate and ion group. In 'Mass labels' mode desaturate the sphere colors toward a neutral gray-blue, show all eight m_i labels plus their coordinate triples, and keep the dashed cube; in 'Ion colors' mode restore full green/red saturation and de-emphasize the coordinate text.

authoredContext:
Solution Define the origin to be at the location of the chloride ion at the bottom left of the unit cell. The figure shows the coordinate system.

A single unit cell of a NaCl crystal.

An illustration of a unit cell of an N a C l crystal as a cube with ions at each corner. Four green ions are shown and labeled as m 1 at the origin, m 3 at the corner on the diagonal on the x y plane, m 6 at the corner on the diagonal on the x z plane, and m 8 at the corner on the diagonal on the y z plane. Four red ions are shown and labeled as m 2 on the x axis, m 4 on the y axis, m 5 on the z axis, and m 7 on the remaining corner.

There are eight ions in this crystal, so N = 8:

attempts.html:
Emphasis
Guided demo
Drag to orbit the cell · scroll to zoom · hover a sphere to read its ion type and coordinates (in units of the edge a).
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Default camera looks almost exactly down a cube body diagonal, so the cell projects to a flat hexagon: m4 (0,a,0) and m6 (a,0,a) land on the same screen point, one sphere is completely hidden and the two labels collide. The source uses a general oblique/axonometric view in which all eight spheres are separated.

Because of that view the y-axis is drawn as a tiny foreshortened stub pointing at the viewer, whereas in the source the y-axis runs clearly to the upper right and visibly passes through the back-bottom corner (m4) — a key depth cue of the original.

The overlapping centre corner renders green (m6 drawn over m4), so the visible centre sphere reads as the wrong ion colour compared with the source, where m4 is unmistakably red and m6 a separate green sphere.
Sphere radius relative to the cube edge is noticeably smaller than in the source (source spheres nearly touch along the edges), making the figure look sparser than the original.
The 'Mass labels' mode recolours all ions to neutral grey-blue, a colour scheme that appears nowhere in the source figure.
evaluation.notes: Correct primitives, ion colouring pattern, dashed cube edges and labelled axes, plus solid interactions (mode toggle, 3-step demo, hover tooltips/guides), but the near-diagonal default camera collapses two corner ions onto one point, hiding m4 and colliding its label with m6, which flattens the cube and departs noticeably from the source view.

feedback.rationale: The concept, primitives, and interaction structure are correct; the issues are implementation details (default camera angle causing corner overlap, sphere radius scale, label collision, grey-blue mass-label palette) that can be fixed in rendering.

discrepancies: The y axis is severely foreshortened in the generated view: its arrowhead lands inside the cube right on top of m4, whereas in the source the y axis extends well beyond the cell to the upper right with a clear, long shaft and arrow.
Several m-labels sit on top of their spheres rather than beside them (m1, m4, m5, m3, m7 are partly occluded by the sphere geometry); in the source every label is offset clearly outside the ion.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept_accuracy 5), but concrete rendering issues—foreshortened y-axis arrow colliding with m4, labels overlapping spheres, and color/size fidelity—are implementation-level fixes.

Solid black axes emerge from a corner labeled 0 at the lower left, with x running toward the lower right, y toward the upper right, and z straight up, each ending in an arrowhead beside its italic label. Dashed orange lines trace the edges of the cube. Eight shaded spheres sit at the corners in two alternating colors, each tagged with a subscripted mass symbol. The green spheres are m_1 at the origin, m_3 at the far corner of the xy face, m_6 at the far corner of the xz face, and m_8 at the far corner of the yz face. The red spheres are m_2 out along the x-axis, m_4 out along the y-axis, m_5 up the z-axis, and m_7 at the corner diagonally opposite the origin. The alternation of the two colors around every face shows that no two like-colored ions share an edge, and numbering all eight corners while anchoring the origin on one of them supplies the labeled coordinates needed to work out the center of mass of the eight-particle cell.

elements: Solid black x-axis from origin running toward lower-right with arrowhead and italic label 'x'
Solid black y-axis from origin running toward upper-right with arrowhead and italic label 'y'
Solid black z-axis from origin running straight up with arrowhead and italic label 'z'
Label '0' at the origin corner (lower-left)
Cube unit cell of side a, one corner exactly at the origin, edges aligned with +x, +y, +z
Twelve cube edges drawn as dashed orange lines (the three edges lying along the axes are overdrawn by the solid black axis lines)
Green sphere m1 at (0,0,0), the origin corner
Red sphere m2 at (a,0,0), out along the x-axis
Green sphere m3 at (a,a,0), far corner of the bottom xy face
Red sphere m4 at (0,a,0), out along the y-axis
Red sphere m5 at (0,0,a), up the z-axis
Green sphere m6 at (a,0,a), far corner of the xz (y=0) face
Red sphere m7 at (a,a,a), the corner diagonally opposite the origin
Green sphere m8 at (0,a,a), far corner of the yz (x=0) face
Subscripted mass labels m1..m8 placed beside each sphere (m5 left of its sphere, m8 above, m7 upper-right, m6 lower-right, m4 right, m3 right, m2 below, m1 below-left)
Soft shading/specular highlight on each sphere giving it a ball-like 3D appearance

interactions.teaches: The eight labeled masses really sit on the corners of one cube; rotating shows which spheres are near versus far and confirms that green and red ions strictly alternate along every edge in all three directions.
Pointing at a corner names that ion, shows its (x, y, z) coordinate in units of the cube edge a, and reports its color group — tying the label m_i to a definite position for the center-of-mass sum.

interactions.label: Emphasis
interactions.teaches: Switching emphasis separates the physical crystal fact — two alternating ion species, no two like ions sharing an edge — from the bookkeeping view, where the same eight corners are just numbered masses with coordinates to feed into the center-of-mass formula.

demo_steps.title: The unit cell on the axes
demo_steps.narration: A cube of edge a sits with one corner at the origin, its edges running along x, y and z. Dashed orange lines outline the cell.

demo_steps.title: Alternating ions
demo_steps.narration: Green and red spheres alternate around every face: m1, m3, m6 and m8 are one species, m2, m4, m5 and m7 the other. No two like-colored ions ever share an edge.

demo_steps.title: Eight masses with coordinates
demo_steps.narration: Now the same corners read as numbered masses m1 through m8. Hover any sphere to see its coordinate — (0,0,0), (a,0,0), (a,a,0), (0,a,0), (0,0,a), (a,0,a), (a,a,a), (0,a,a) — the data needed for the center-of-mass sum.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cube edge a = 2.0 world units, corner m1 at the world origin, cube occupying x,y,z in [0,2]. Axes are solid black lines from the origin out to 3.0 units along +x (screen lower-right), +y (screen upper-right) and +z (screen up), each capped with a small cone arrowhead and an italic label just past the tip. Corner coordinates in units of a: m1(0,0,0) green, m2(1,0,0) red, m3(1,1,0) green, m4(0,1,0) red, m5(0,0,1) red, m6(1,0,1) green, m7(1,1,1) red, m8(0,1,1) green. Sphere radius ≈ 0.22 (about 11% of the edge), all eight equal. Colors: green ions #7CB342 with lighter #A5D66B highlight; red ions #C0392B with #E06055 highlight; cube edges dashed orange #E8642A (dash ~0.12, gap ~0.10); axes, arrowheads and text black #111111. Center of mass, if shown, is at (a/2, a/2, a/2) only when all eight masses are equal; otherwise R = (Σ m_i r_i)/(Σ m_i). Label offsets follow the source: m5 to the left of its sphere, m8 above, m7 upper-right, m6 lower-right, m4 to the right, m3 to the right, m2 below, m1 below-left, and '0' just left of the origin.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera in a standard isometric pose so cube edges stay parallel, matching the flat drafting look of the source. Spheres: MeshStandardMaterial with moderate roughness plus one key directional light from the upper left and a soft ambient fill to reproduce the shaded-ball look. Dashed cube edges: LineSegments with LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) — draw all twelve edges dashed, then overlay the three origin-adjacent edges with the solid black axis lines so the axes read on top. Labels as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so subscripts render crisply and always face the camera during orbit. Hover: raycast against the eight sphere meshes; on hit, scale the sphere ~1.25x, add an emissive rim, drop faint guide lines to its x, y and z axis projections, and show a tooltip with the mass symbol, coordinate and ion group. In 'Mass labels' mode desaturate the sphere colors toward a neutral gray-blue, show all eight m_i labels plus their coordinate triples, and keep the dashed cube; in 'Ion colors' mode restore full green/red saturation and de-emphasize the coordinate text.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Hover over a corner sphere: learner points to m1 through m8; that ion, its coordinate relative to the origin, and its color group highlight; the connection between labels, positions, and the center-of-mass setup becomes clear without crowding the cube.
- Toggle between ion colors and mass labels: learner switches emphasis between species coloring and numbered masses; the visible update either stresses red-green alternation along edges or the coordinate bookkeeping for eight particles; the difference between crystal pattern and calculation data becomes clear.

discrepancies: The y-axis is drawn far too short on screen: its arrowhead terminates inside the cube next to m6 rather than emerging well beyond the far top-right corner as in the source, so the 'y' label collides with the 'm6' label and the axis reads as an interior diagonal.

The blue centre-of-mass label 'R' is visible in the default view even though the R marker sphere and its guide lines are hidden (checkbox unticked) — a stray annotation with no corresponding geometry.

Axis extents are inconsistent with the source: in the printed figure all three axes overshoot the cube generously (z rises clearly above m8, x well past m2); here the z arrow barely clears m5/m8 and the overall axis frame is cramped relative to the cell.
Ion labels sit noticeably further from their spheres than in the source (e.g. m4, m6, m3 offsets), which makes a couple of associations ambiguous where labels land near neighbouring geometry.

The 'Mass labels' mode recolours all spheres to muted grey-blue, abandoning the source's green/red alternation; this is an added mode not in the original and changes the figure's signature colour scheme when active.
evaluation.notes: A faithful axonometric reconstruction of the ionic unit cell with correct corner colouring, dashed orange edges, solid black axes and complete m1–m8 labelling, plus genuinely useful toggles, a centre-of-mass marker and a 3-step demo; the main weaknesses are a badly foreshortened/truncated y-axis whose arrow and label crowd m6, and a stray 'R' label shown while its marker is hidden.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are implementation details like axis lengths, label offsets, and a stray 'R' annotation tied to a hidden marker.
